reference_sql:
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('week', order_date) AS DATE) AS week_start,
       SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur
FROM sales
WHERE order_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY date_trunc('week', order_date)
alternatives: SELECT order_week AS week_start, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur FROM sales WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY order_week
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('week', order_date) AS DATE) AS week_start, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur FROM sales WHERE year(order_date) = 2025 AND month(order_date) = 12 GROUP BY 1

other_way.sql: SELECT order_week AS week_start, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur FROM sales WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY order_week
other_way.tradeoff: The view's order_week column already holds each line's week Monday, but date_trunc works on any date column.

solver.query:
SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date)::DATE AS week_start, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur
FROM sales
WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND order_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY 1
